State of Maine
STATE BOARD OF EDUCATION
Testimony of Fern Desj ardins, Chair of the State Board of Education
In Support of: L.D. 323: An Act to Fund Staff Support for the State Board of Education.
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs
Sponsored by: Representative Brennan
Date: March 18, 2025
Senator Rafferty, Representative Kelly Murphy, and Honorable Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs:
My name is Fern Desjardins, Chair of the Maine State Board of Education. I welcome this
opportunity to submit testimony on behalf of the State Board in support of L.D. 323: An Act to
Fund Staff Support for the State Board of Education. As a retired educator, I've served on the State Board for almost seven years and been honored to serve as chair since July 1, 2021.
It would have been challenging for me to serve on the State Board, especially as chair of the Board, while I was employed in any of the positions I held during my PK-12 career in
education. Board members have only one staff member, an office specialist, to assist them in their work. The workload of members is much heavier than that of other boards I've served on.
Allow me to review the Board's composition and some of their responsibilities.
The State Board has 11 members, 9 voting members and two non-voting students. Voting members are elected for a 5-year term and can serve two terms. In 2026, 4 members' terms will expire; in 2027, 2 members' terms; and in 2028, 3 members' terms will expire. Some may be appointed to serve a second term; others won't be reappointed or will term out. Having 4 out of 9 members get off the Board in any given year is certainly not good for the Board.
Since I began serving as chair of the State Board, I've worked with three secretary/office
specialists in a period of 3 years, 8 months. In fact, the Board is currently assisting the MDOE
in filling the vacancy of the office specialist that recently resigned. When 2026 rolls around, the Board will have a new chair with 6 months experience in that role, an office specialist with 8
months experience, and 4 members' terms up for reappointment.
Two of the eight characteristics of an online AI overview of effective organizations are
Effective Leadership and Operational Excellence. The State Board is led by its chair - a position that is voted on amually. Since July 1, 1999:
4 chairs served for 1 year; 2 chairs served for 2 years; 2 chairs served for 3 years; and 3 chairs will have served for 4 years by June 30, 2025.
With the leadership changing every 1-4 years, how can the Board keep its vision in the
forefront to achieve ambitious goals, anticipate challenges, make informed decisions, and

empower board members by providing resources and fostering a sense of ownership and
responsibility? The resources provided to Board members are the services of the MDOE and, to
a limited extent, the National Association of State Boards of Education.
Efficiency, quality, and continuous improvement are key to Operational Excellence. Continuous improvement is especially challenging for a volunteer board without consistent
leadership. Some of our policies need to be updated. Rule Chapter ll4 needs to be amended, but Rule Chapter 115 has consumed much of the work of the Certification and Higher
Education Committee since 2017. Other rules of the Board that need to be reviewed are
Chapter ll9, Chapter 138, Chapter 149, Chapter 170, and Chapter 301. And it would be good
for the Board to actually have the support needed to carry out certain duties in 20-A MRSA
such as �405(3)(S) on developing "long-range education goals and standards for school performance and student performance to improve learning results ... and recommend to the commissioner and to the Legislature a plan for achieving those goals and standards."
A few examples of questions to consider regarding the work of the State Board would include:
1. ls it reasonable to expect volunteers on a board to carry out the responsibilities in 20-A
MRSA �40l-A, powers and duties in �405, and adopt rules to carry out its responsibilities
with only an office specialist on staff to assist?
2. Should a volunteer chair be responsible for new member orientation, website updates,
ensuring public notice is given for all Board and committee meetings, minutes being recorded, training members for Educator Preparation Program reviews in accordance with
Rule Chapter ll4, and even following the requirements of the Bureau of Human Resources
in evaluating the performance of the office specialist?
3. Is it reasonable to expect a volunteer Board member to prepare an 8-year report - the
Govermnent Evaluation Act Program Evaluation Report -- for the State Board of Education?
Members of the State Board are volunteers. Some do not have the capacity to directly manage and oversee operating, support or administrative functions of the Board. The only assistance the
Board receives is from an office specialist with limited to no financial training or leadership
capacity. From my experience as chair for almost four years, the State Board would be in a
better position if it had a full-time executive director and part-time administrative assistant to help carry out its responsibilities and duties. That is the staffing for the Delaware State Board
of Education, and they speak positively of the 1.5 FTE staff positions.
An Executive Director would provide visionary leadership and management of the State
Board's programs and initiatives in collaboration with key educational stakeholder groups, and
serve as the primary liaison Board representative to the MDOE, Governor's office, legislature, LEA's and professional groups. An Executive Director would provide continuity to the work of
the State Board and build upon prior accomplishments while addressing identified needs.
The State Board supports L.D. 323 for what it could do toward enhancing the Board's effectiveness in meeting more of its responsibilities and duties.
Thank you for this opportunity to comment, and l would be happy to answer questions the
committee may have.

Testimony ofRepresentative Michael Brennan presenting
LD 323, An Act to Fund Staff Support for the State Board of Education
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Aflairs
Good afternoon, Senator Rafferty, Representative Noonen Murphy and fellow distinguished
members of the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs. My name is
Michael Brennan, and I represent House District 115, which includes a portion of Portland.
Today, I am here to introduce LD 323, An Act to Fund Staff Support for the State Board of
Education.
This is a very simple bill. LD 323 provides ongoing funds of $100,000 over the course of two
fiscal years for the State Board of Education to contract for staffing services.
The Maine State Board of Education serves in an advisory capacity to the Commissioner of Education regarding our state education laws. Further, the Board makes policy recommendations to the legislative and executive branches.
Additionally, the Board's responsibilities include overseeing approval of school construction projects, administering federal funds awarded to Maine for career and teclmical education, establishing standards for teacher certification, approving educator preparation programs as well as recommending institutions of higher education for degree-granting authority.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I am happy to answer any questions.

Testimony of Dr. Thomas Keller, member of the Maine State Board of Education and Chair of the Certification and Higher Education Committee in Favor of LD 323 An Act to Fund Support for the State Board of Education.

March 16, 2025

Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy, and distinguished members ofthe Joint Standing Committee on
Education and Cultural Affairs. My name is Tom Keller and lam a member of the Maine State Board of Education and lam chair of its Certification and Higher Education Committee. I am testifying in Favor of LD 323
--An Act to Fund Staff Support for the State Board of Education.

Pursuant to Section 401 of Title 20-A, the State Board of Education is "intended to act as a body with certain

policy-making, administrative and advisory functions. In those capacities, the board has the primary

responsibility for the fol/owing:

1. Formulating policy. Formulating policy by which the commissioner shall administer certain regulatory

tasks;
2. Advising commissioner.
of that position; and

Advising the commissioner in the administration of all the mandated responsibilities
'

3. Enforcing regulatory requirements. Enforcing regulatory requirements for school administrative units.

The state board may advise the commissioner and the Legislature on matters concerning state laws relating to
public preschool to grade 12 and postsecondary education."
The responsibilities of the State Board are numerous and important. The Board, which is an autonomous body, is meant to have staff assistance from the Maine Department of Education in carrying out our functions. There are slots for nine voting members and two nonvoting student members, all appointed by the Governor following review by this committee and confirmation by the Senate. At present, we have a full-time Office Specialist as our only support.

Title 20-A identifies 20 specific duties of the Board which are generally reflected in our three major committees: the Career and Technical Education Committee, Certification and Higher Education Committee, and School Construction Committee. The Board also has a Student Voice Committee, Student Membership Committee, and Legislative Action Committee.

The Career and Technical Education Committee (CTE Committee) is the cognizant organization in Maine for the
federal Carl D. Perkins funds, totaling over $5M in FY25. We work closely with Maine Department of Education
staff, primarily Dwight Littlefield, in allocating these funds to the 27 CTE centers.

The Certification and Higher Education Committee (C&HE Committee) oversees implementation of Chapter 114 Purpose, Standards and Procedures for the Review and Approval of Educational Personnel Preparation Programs, Chapter 115 The Credentialing of Education Personnel, Chapter 149 Procedures for Obtaining Authorization for Institutions of Higher Education to Confer Academic Degrees or to offer Degree Courses/Programs in the State of Maine, and Chapter 170 Evaluating Requests for Degree Authorization (Maine
and Out-of-State Institutions). We works closely with Maine Department of Education staff, primarily Michael
Perry, in all phases of educator certification, review of educational preparation programs, and degree granting
authority.
The School Construction Committee oversees all aspects of new school construction, which these days are
running around $900/square foot and the total construction cost of a single school is millions of dollars. We

work closely with Maine Department of Education staff, primarily Scott Brown, on all phases of school
construction.
To summarize, the State Board oversees millions of dollars in education spending, all teacher, administrator, and educational specialist certifications, and degrees offered by Maine's higher education institutions. All with 9 volunteers and a single administrative support person.
_
As comparison, the lvlaine Charter School Commission, which oversees 10 slots for public charter schools and
some 2,700 students has 3 staff members including an executive director, a research analyst and a business manager and funds for hiring specialty consultants. The Maine State Board of Nursing has 8 staff members including an executive director and an assistant executive director. There are approximately the same number as nurses as there are teachers in Maine. The Maine State Board of Environmental Protection has at least a
Board Executive Analyst and a Board Clerk.
Should this bill pass Ought to Pass out of committee, there is still the price tag to consider. ln this fiscal climate, I recognize that $100,000 per year for two years is a sizable amount. And, truly, this would likely fund a .5 FTE
Executive Director. But we have worked to create a job description (FJA) for an executive director position already. In fact we have proposed this as part of our budget request the past two years and that request was
not supported by the executive branch.
I would request that if the full amount cannot be appropriated, that at least half of that amount be appropriated and that we be allowed to use that for two purposes.
One purpose is to convene task forces on particular topics. We could convene educators to examine promising
practices such as the paying of student teachers, further instruction for pre-service teachers in the science of
reading, mathematics and science, and the training of mentor teachers. We could catalyze collaboration in the
p|<~20 system of education in Maine. Regular meetings of the SBE chair and vice chair (and future executive
director), ECA Committee chairs, the commissioner of the MDOE, the Governor's education aid, the chancellor
of the UMS and the president of the state community college system to coordinate and collaborate should occur and should include the public. We could gather and disseminate staff information from those in new buildings who have informed opinions on what works and what doesn't in new construction, which would be
extremely beneficial to those districts building new schools.
A second purpose is to add funds to our Revenue budget line. We are told that without a certain amount of
funds in this line, we are prohibited from accepting grant funds. The SBE wrote a proposal with full cooperation of the MDOE and was granted $10,000. We had to refuse the grant since we did not have a line in our budget
allowing receipt of grant funds and the MDOE refused to be the fiscal agent. We need authority to accept grant
funds.
We urge that you support passage of LD 323 -- An Act to Fund Staff Support for the State Board of Education
and give us resources we need to fulfill our responsibilities and duties.
lam happy to address any questions you have.
Thank you.
